holidays.name: National Watermelon Day
holidays.description: A juicy celebration of the summer fruit that is 92 percent water. Fans slice, spit seeds, and chow down on everything from classic wedges to watermelon pizza and feta salads.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States as an unofficial food holiday, it was popularized by food-holiday calendars and has long been tied to the peak of watermelon season in early August.
holidays.funFact: In Japan, farmers have grown cube-shaped watermelons by cultivating them in square glass boxes, and they can sell for hundreds of dollars.

holidays.name: National Grab Some Nuts Day
holidays.description: A cheeky snack-themed day encouraging people to grab a handful of nuts, whether almonds, pistachios, cashews, or peanuts. Expect plenty of puns and trail mix.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance spread through food-holiday calendars and social media, built on the snack's wordplay and the nutritional appeal of nuts.
holidays.funFact: Peanuts are not true nuts at all. They are legumes that grow underground, making them cousins of beans and lentils.

holidays.name: National Georgia Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the Peach State with peach cobbler, Southern hospitality, and a nod to its famous Atlanta skyline and sweet tea.
holidays.origin: Georgia’s ties to peaches and Southern culture inspired this regional observance, which circulates on state-pride and unofficial holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Despite the nickname, Georgia is not the top U.S. peach producer. California grows far more peaches, while Georgia keeps the nickname.

holidays.name: National White Wine Day
holidays.description: Wine lovers pop corks on chardonnay, sauvignon blanc, riesling, and pinot grigio. It's a perfect excuse for a chilled glass on a warm summer evening.
holidays.origin: A modern unofficial drinks holiday created by beverage and wine enthusiasts and spread widely through social media and holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: White wine can be made from red grapes, because the juice of most red grapes is clear and the color comes from the skins.

holidays.name: International Beer Day (First Friday of August)
holidays.description: A global toast to brewers, bartenders, and beer fans, celebrated with tastings, brewery visits, and cheers to friends around the world.
holidays.origin: Started in 2007 in Santa Cruz, California by Jesse Avshalomov, it grew into an international event celebrated in dozens of countries, usually held on the first Friday of August.
holidays.funFact: The holiday has three stated goals: gather with friends, celebrate the people who brew and serve beer, and unite the world under beer from every nation.
